title_ar: استخدام وسائل التقنية الحديثة أثناء أداء مناسك الحج
title_en: Using Modern Technology While Performing the Rites of Hajj
body_ar: الشيخ الدّدو لقناة الجزيرة: {لا حرج في استخدام وسائل التقنية الحديثة فيما هو نافع للحاج ومعين له على اداء نسكه دون إسراف } الحمد لله والصلاة والسلام على نبينا محمد وعلى آله واصحابه أجمعين ، أما بعد فإن هذه الوسائل هي من نعم الله سبحانه وتعالى التي أنعم بها على عباده ؛فإذا صرفوها فيما يرضيه وما يقرب اليه كانت عونا على الطاعة ، ولا ينبغي الاسراف فيه وتجاوز الحد ، لكن لا حرج في استعمالها فيما هو نافع ومعين للحاج على اداء نسكه وفي تحديد اوقاته وفي تحديد السير وعلاماته وغير ذلك مما ينظم شؤون الحياة ؛ فهي امور يحتاج الناس اليها ومن نعمة الله ان أنعم بها في هذا الوقت الذي كثر فيه الناس وكثرت فيه وسائل الاتصال وكثرت فيه وسائل النقل واستطاع كثير من الناس الحج ؛ ففي اوقات مضت لم يكن هذا الكم من الناس يستطيع الوصول إلى المناسك والمشاعر ولا أداءها في وقت واحد ، فلذلك احتيج إلى هذه الوسائل في التواصل بين الحجيج ؛ففي السنوات الماضية كنا نشاهد ضياع كثير من الضعفة الذين ليس لهم من يرعاهم ، وبعضهم لا يؤدي نسكه أصلا فلا يقف بعرفة . واليوم بحمد الله اصبح من الممكن الوصول إلى كل انسان في مكانه الذي هو فيه ان استغل هذه الوسائل لذلك بالصوت والصورة. • كيف تستفيد الأمة من اجتماع كهذا ..أكثر من مليوني حاج في موسم مهيب؟الشيخ حفظه الله: الحج هو مؤتمر الأمة السنوي الكبيرُ الذي افترضه الله سبحانه وتعالى وجعله ركنا من أركان الإسلام يجتمع فيه قاصي المسلمين ودانِيهم ، ومشرقيُّهم ومغربيُّهم ، وعربيهم وعجميهم يلبسون زيا موحدا ويلهجون بذكر موحد ، ويسلكون هذه المسالك التي سلكها أنبياء الله من قبل وسلكها أبونا إبراهيم عليه السلام وأحياها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال: " خذوا عني مناسككم " فأثر الحج لذلك عظيم من عدة وجوه :- الوجه الأول : أنه يكفر سيئات الحاضرين ويغير حياتهم وسلوكهم فالأمة محتاجة إلى أن يكون فيها عدد من المغفور لهم ترجى دعواتهم وتستجاب ، وهي محتاجة إلى تغيير السلوك فهو بمثابة تغيير الدماء كما إذا أخذ الدم من الإنسان واعيد إليه من جديد بالتغذية - كما أن من فوائد الحج أن فيه اطلاعا على أحوال المسلمين في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها وهذا أمر تشاركون فيه انتم رجال الإعلام وفرسان الأقلام، ولكن ليس من رءا كمن سمع فنحن الآن نلتقي أناسا قدموا من بورما وناسا جاءوا من اليمن وناسا جاءوا من اماكن شتى كلها فيها جراح للمسلمين نابضة ، والمسلمون في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها مطالبون بالشعور بآلام إخوانهم فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:" المؤمن للمؤمن كالبنيان يشد بعضه بعضا وشبك بين أصابعه " ويقول صلى الله عليه وسلم:" مثل المؤمنين في توادهم وتراحمهم وتعاطفهم كمثل الجسد إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالحمى والسهر".. فلا يمكن أن يقع ذلك إلا بهذا التعارف في هذا المؤتمر ..وإذا رجعوا بإذن الله سيرجع كل واحد منهم بما رءا وسمع وينقله نقلا مباشرا ويؤدي ذلك إلى زيادة الأخوة بين المسلين وتقوية الترابط بينهم.
body_en:
Sheikh al-Dedew to Al Jazeera: "There is no objection to using modern technological means in what is of benefit to the pilgrim and assists him in performing his rite, without extravagance."

Praise be to God, and prayers and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions, all of them. To proceed:

These means are among the blessings of God, glorified and exalted, which He has bestowed upon His servants. If they turn them to what pleases Him and what brings them near to Him, they are a help towards obedience. There should be no extravagance in this and no overstepping of the limit; but there is no objection to using them in what is of benefit and assists the pilgrim in performing his rite, in fixing its times, in determining the route and its markers, and in other things by which the affairs of life are ordered. These are matters people need, and it is part of God's favour that He has bestowed them at this time — a time in which people have become many, the means of communication have become many, the means of transport have become many, and many people have become able to perform the hajj. In times past this number of people could not have reached the rites and the sacred sites, nor performed them all at one time; and for that reason these means became needed for communication among the pilgrims. In past years we used to see many of the weak, who have no one to look after them, going astray, and some of them not performing their rite at all, so that they would not stand at Arafat. Today, praise be to God, it has become possible to reach every person in the place where he is, if these means are used for that, by voice and by image.

• How is the community to benefit from a gathering such as this — more than two million pilgrims in an awe-inspiring season?

The Sheikh (may God preserve him): The hajj is the community's great annual conference, which God, glorified and exalted, made obligatory and made a pillar of Islam. In it the far and the near among the Muslims come together, their easterners and their westerners, their Arabs and their non-Arabs. They wear one dress and give voice to one remembrance, and they walk these paths that the prophets of God walked before them, that our father Abraham (peace be upon him) walked, and that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) revived, when he said: "Take from me your rites."

The effect of the hajj is therefore immense, in several respects.

The first respect: that it wipes away the misdeeds of those present and changes their lives and their conduct. The community needs to have within it a number of people who have been forgiven, whose supplications are hoped for and answered; and it needs a change of conduct. It is like a changing of the blood, as when blood is taken from a person and restored to him anew through nourishment.

— Another of the benefits of the hajj is that in it there is an acquaintance with the conditions of the Muslims in the east and the west of the earth. This is something you take part in, you men of the media and knights of the pen; but the one who has seen is not like the one who has heard. We are meeting now people who have come from Burma, people who have come from Yemen, people who have come from various places, in all of which there are throbbing wounds of the Muslims. The Muslims in the east and the west of the earth are required to feel the pains of their brothers, for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) says: "The believer to the believer is like a building, one part of it supporting another" — and he interlaced his fingers. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) says: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, their mutual mercy and their mutual compassion is the likeness of the body: when one limb of it complains, the rest of the body answers it with fever and sleeplessness."

That cannot come about except through this mutual acquaintance at this conference. And when they return, God willing, each one of them will return with what he has seen and heard and will convey it directly, and that will lead to an increase of brotherhood among the Muslims and a strengthening of the bonds between them.

flags.arabic: {لا حرج في استخدام وسائل التقنية الحديثة … دون إسراف }
options: a pull-quote from the interview, set off by the site in braces
flags.note: SOURCE FORMATTING. The source encloses the headline pull-quote in curly braces, which in this corpus are reserved for Qur'anic text (style guide section 4). It is not scripture; it is the Sheikh's own sentence, which recurs almost verbatim in the body. The English puts it in ordinary quotation marks and the Arabic is preserved as the source has it. Whoever cleans the corpus globally should be aware that braces in body_ar are not a reliable marker of scripture.

flags.arabic: فهو بمثابة تغيير الدماء كما إذا أخذ الدم من الإنسان واعيد إليه من جديد بالتغذية
flags.context: the image for the change of conduct the hajj brings about
options: like a changing of the blood, as when blood is taken from a person and restored to him anew through nourishment
like a transfusion, where blood is drawn from a person and replaced after he has been fed
the image is compressed in transcription and its mechanism is unclear
flags.note: The simile is elliptical as transcribed and the third option may be the truth of it. Rendered as literally as English allows, without being turned into a modern transfusion, which the Arabic does not say.

flags.context: كنا نشاهد ضياع كثير من الضعفة الذين ليس لهم من يرعاهم
options: many of the weak going astray, that is, getting lost
many of the weak being lost, that is, perishing
many of the weak being neglected
flags.note: ضياع covers both getting lost and being lost. The following clause — that some did not perform the rite at all and so did not stand at Arafat — points to getting lost rather than dying, which is why the first reading is taken.

flags.context: زيادة الأخوة بين المسلين; ليس من رءا كمن سمع
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECTS (house rule 11): a dropped letter in المسلمين and a non-standard spelling of رأى, both twice over. Preserved unchanged in body_ar and translated normally. The record also carries a scattering of missing hamzas (اداء, اوقاته, امور, انتم) which are not individually flagged.

translator_notes: This is an interview with Al Jazeera, not a written fatwa, although the CMS files it under the written-fatwas category. Typed 'transcript'. Two questions and answers are published; whether the interview ran longer cannot be told from the record.
The two prophetic reports quoted at the end are given without narrator, collection or grading, as he gives them. None has been added.
The Sheikh's ruling on the use of technology is 'there is no objection' (لا حرج), qualified by 'without extravagance' — not one of the five rulings, and not rendered as 'permissible (mubāḥ)'.
The references to Burma and Yemen are his own and are translated as given, without gloss or context.
